question: Can the explicit Yabahan River localities in DENR and EMB records be linked to the current PSA PSGC municipality codes without asserting river route or exact reach geometry?
method: Reused the reviewed source row in the existing DENR/EMB river-name crosswalk, then matched only its printed locality names to the current PSA municipality directory. Replaced the single province-only association with two source-described locality associations, retaining distinct source attribution for the historical San Francisco locality. Neither assignment is a route or feature-boundary claim.

assignments.limit: Historical locality text is recorded verbatim as a source-described administrative context; the municipality code does not establish which reach lies in San Francisco or define channel geometry.

limitations: The EMB table is historical and prints “QUEZNON”; the existing source review treats this as a typographic error in a Quezon report context, but the spelling is preserved rather than silently corrected in the quoted source row.
The PSA codes identify municipalities only; they are not river centerlines, waterbody boundaries, municipal-water boundaries, or proof of continuous channel passage through both localities.
The 2026 Quezon advisory spelling “Yabahaan” remains crosswalked at river-name/locality level only; its exact reach remains unresolved.
The DENR class B listing is regulatory classification context, not current ambient water quality, fish habitat, or safety guidance.
No fish presence or absence, abundance, geometry, salinity, access, fishing rule, hazard, species assertion, or public-app record is added.

decisions.decision: Retain the existing river lead; link San Andres to the DENR and historical EMB locality wording, and San Francisco only to the historical EMB locality wording. Keep the source-era reach and route unresolved.

nextAction: Continue the CALABARZON locality queue using explicit source-named LGU contexts; keep exact waterbody geometry and site-resolved fish evidence as separate workstreams.
